Visions and Values
AYLWARD PRIMARY SCHOOL MOTTO
Inspire, Enjoy, Achieve
To fulfil this vision, all members of the school community should:
Aylward provides an environment where children:
Visions and Values
Feel safe, secure, and included.
Feel valued, respected and treated fairly.
Are treated as individuals.
Can achieve their best.
Are encouraged to have high aspirations.
Become confident, determined and independent learners.
Celebrate uniqueness and diversity.
Our School values
Our five school values: Kindness, Determination, Respect, Honesty and Responsibility are at the heart of school life at Aylward. They underpin our expectations and behaviour policy, guiding how we learn, grow and treat one another as a school community.
Each value has its own mascot, helping us introduce these important concepts in an engaging and memorable way. Through assemblies, our approach to learning and everyday school life, we encourage everyone in our school community to understand and put these values into practice
Meet ouR MASCOTS:
British Values
At Aylward, we uphold and promote British Values through our behaviour policy and expectations, a range of school events and activities, and our PSHE curriculum. These provide opportunities for pupils to develop an understanding of the values that underpin our society and to consider how they can be demonstrated in their own lives.
For further information about how British Values are promoted at Aylward, please see our British Values Policy below.

Welcome
Welcome to Aylward Primary School
What I love most about Aylward is the sense of community we build from the very start of you joining our Aylward family.
On behalf of the staff, children, parents and governors, I am delighted to welcome you to Aylward Primary School.
At Aylward, we believe every child should feel valued, inspired and empowered to achieve their very best. We are proud to be a welcoming and inclusive school community where children are encouraged to be ambitious, develop confidence in themselves and discover their individual strengths and talents.
Our aim is not simply to educate children academically, but to provide experiences that broaden horizons, spark curiosity and prepare children for life beyond primary school. We want our children to leave Aylward as resilient, thoughtful and compassionate young people with a love of learning and the confidence to embrace future opportunities.
We recognise that children flourish when they feel safe, happy and supported. Therefore, alongside delivering a broad, ambitious and engaging curriculum, we place great importance on wellbeing, inclusion and ensuring that every child feels a strong sense of belonging. We celebrate the rich diversity of our school community and are committed to ensuring that all children, regardless of background, need or starting point, are given every opportunity to succeed.
At Aylward, learning extends far beyond the classroom. Through enrichment opportunities, clubs, educational visits, wider experiences and leadership opportunities, we aim to ignite passions, develop talents and create lasting memories. We have high expectations for all members of our community and believe that challenge, encouragement and support help children to achieve more than they ever thought possible.
Strong relationships sit at the heart of everything we do. We value the partnership between home and school and believe children achieve their greatest success when families and staff work together. We are proud of the supportive and positive community we have built and of the opportunities we create for parents and carers to play an active role in school life.
Our website will give you a flavour of life at Aylward, but nothing compares to experiencing our school in person. We warmly welcome prospective families to visit us and see first-hand the enthusiasm, kindness and ambition that make Aylward such a special place.
I feel incredibly proud to lead such a dedicated and caring school community and look forward to welcoming you and your family to Aylward Primary School.
Please click here for further information regarding School Tours and meeting the HeadTeacher, Mrs Kelly.

Wraparound Childcare
At Aylward Primary School, we recognise the importance of providing families with flexible, high-quality childcare that supports them before and after the school day, as well as during school holidays.
Our Breakfast Club (ABC) is available from 8.00am, providing children with a welcoming start to the school day. Our After School Club (PAALS) runs until 5.45pm, giving families flexibility at the end of the school day. Both services provide children with a safe and enjoyable environment in which to spend time with their friends and take part in a range of activities.
For our Nursery children, we also offer 30 hours of funded childcare for eligible working parents, alongside the option for families who do not qualify for the funding to pay for full-time Nursery provision. Please see our Admissions page for further information.
During the school holidays, our World Club Sports provides children with opportunities to enjoy a varied programme of activities, using our extensive school facilities. Activities include football, basketball, gymnastics, yoga, mindfulness, badminton, woodland games, bushcraft, Forest School, arts and crafts, drama, dance and story-time, alongside many other sporting and creative activities. The Holiday Club is open to children from Aylward and other schools, providing families with an additional option for holiday childcare.
Our wraparound provision is designed to provide safe, engaging and enriching experiences for children, while giving parents and carers the flexibility and reassurance they need to balance school, work and family commitments.

Music Tuition
At Aylward Primary School, we believe that music is an important part of a broad and enriching education. We provide pupils with opportunities to develop their musical skills, confidence and enjoyment of music through both curriculum learning and instrumental tuition.
Pupils in Years 3 to 6 have the opportunity to learn a musical instrument through small-group tuition provided by teachers from the Harrow Music Service. A range of instruments is available, including violin, flute, guitar, piano and trumpet, subject to sufficient numbers and availability.
Link to Harrow Music Service
We also offer opportunities for our younger pupils in Years 1 and 2 to take part in small-group music tuition through Rock Steady Music, giving children an opportunity to develop their musical interests from an early age.
Link to Rock Steady Music
Instrumental tuition is designed to encourage children to develop their practical musical skills and gives them the opportunity to practise and perform as they progress. Where appropriate, instruments such as violins, flutes and trumpets may be available to hire from the school for the first year, helping pupils to get started. Guitar and piano pupils require access to an appropriate instrument for practice at home.
Through our music provision, we aim to ensure that pupils have the opportunity to discover a love of music, develop their talents and experience the enjoyment and confidence that comes from learning to play an instrument.

READING
At Aylward, we are determined that every pupil will learn to read and develop a life-long love of reading. We do this by prioritising reading and promoting books in as many ways as possible. As a school, we are always thinking of new ways to encourage the children to pick up a book and read.
In Reception and Year 1, phonics is taught systematically, using the Read, Write, Inc (RWI) programme. RWI is lively and challenging. It ensures that children learn to read quickly and that they enjoy reading right from the start. There are also intervention phonics groups in Key Stage 2 to support those who need extra help with their reading and writing. All of the children on the RWI programme take home RWI ‘book bag’ books which closely match the sounds/phonemes they are learning in school. By reading and re-reading these books at home, the children are able to practise and re-enforce what they have been taught at school.
Reading from Year 2 upwards
From Year 2 upwards, the children have daily lessons which focus on comprehension skills. During the lessons, they develop a range of skills including discussing word choice, unlocking the meaning of whole texts and critical appreciation. In KS2 Reading is taught using the Destination Reader framework, which ensures a wide range of skills are taught explicitly. This framework involves using quality, whole-class texts that promote a love of Reading while also ensuring that our pupils have the skills necessary to access and understand a wide range of texts.
Workshops are run to help parents support their child’s reading development. At these workshops, parents find out about how Reading is taught and promoted at school, as well as how they can support their children at home.
When children have reached the end of the RWI programme, they will take a colour-banded book home to read. These book bands are selected based on the child’s word-reading and comprehension level, and pupils are listened to read regularly.
Reading across the curriculum
Every day, teachers read from a quality text to their class, which forms our daily story time. These texts are carefully chosen to inspire and engage pupils and promote reading for pleasure.
During English lessons, teachers read a wide variety of text types with the children: fiction, non-fiction, short stories, reports, diaries, poems etc. This ensures that pupils are continually exposed to quality texts and are given plenty of opportunities to read a variety of text-types and styles. Often, books related to topics the children are learning about in Learning Enquiry or Science, are used to inspire pupils’ writing.
Teachers also regularly use ‘blue project box’ books, to help broaden the children’s knowledge of topics and to develop research skills. These are books provided by the Harrow Library Service.
At Aylward, we have a beautiful, organised and well-stocked school library. Once a week, each class visits the library to take out books. During their time in the library, the children listen to their class teacher reading a story while they select books in groups. Our library books have been grouped into bands, which helps the children to select an accessible text for themselves. In addition, the children use their ‘bookmarks’ to look for recommended texts and to check whether their book is right for them. The bookmark has a series of questions and prompts to help children think about their book selection. We provide an ‘Open Library’ time before school, every Tuesday, for children to enjoy reading with their parents. These sessions are run by our ‘mini-librarians’.
At Aylward, we have enjoyed a range of author visits and workshops, including visits from Stewart Ross, John Dougherty and the young author H.G. Sansostri. Our pupils always enjoy meeting authors and are often inspired to write their own stories afterwards.
Alongside this, we run a range of events to promote reading across the school each year. In KS1 we have a ‘Bedtime Stories’ event and in KS2 there is the ‘Book Cinema’, both of which are very popular among the children. Various competitions are run, including ‘extreme reading’, and we hold events for World Book Day each year. We also take part in the Junior Book Award.
Additionally, each term parents are invited into their children’s classrooms for a ‘Family Reading Morning’ where they share stories together.

SCIENCE
At Aylward, we aim to enrich the lives of our pupils by teaching the Science National Curriculum in an informative and practical way. We aim to teach key working scientifically skills, knowledge, and unit specific vocabulary to raise our pupil’s aspirations and love and enjoyment of Science. We believe that Science is important as it forms the basis of the world that we live in today.
Our whole curriculum is shaped by our school vision, which aims to enable all children, regardless of background, ability, additional needs, to flourish to become the very best scientists and have the best scientific approach they can be.
We teach the National Curriculum which is supported by a clear, sequential progression of scientific based skills and knowledge, building upon prior learning. We also have a dedicated unit of teaching developing Science Capital and working scientifically skills.
During the year, all children will have the opportunity to access and be involved with a range of activities, both in school, the classroom, and externally in form of trips and workshops, linking with their Science work, in addition to a dedicated Science Investigation Day during the year. We have worked hard on raising the profile of Science at Aylward and we take pride in pupils developing their love of Science.
By the time children leave Aylward, they will:
· Be aware of a range of different professions within the Science field;
· Be able to work scientifically and have a scientific approach to their work;
· Be able to discuss their Science learning with reference and association to Science enrichment in form of trips and workshops;
· Exhibit a love of learning by raising their own questions and hypotheses, leading to pupils leading their own investigations and developing their own knowledge and skills at home.

Workshops for Parents
At Aylward, we believe that the strongest outcomes for children happen when school and homework together. Parents and carers know their children best, while our staff bring professional knowledge and expertise. By sharing these perspectives, communicating openly and building positive relationships, we can create a consistent and supportive experience for every child.
We want parents and carers to feel that they are active partners in their child’s education, with meaningful opportunities to get involved, share their views, contribute to school life and work alongside us to support learning and wellbeing.
Please see our Home/School Partnership Calendar and Overview to see events across the academic year.
